question:
The company president was being extorted and had to deliver a ransom during a hostage exchange. The extortionists demanded a specific amount substantially greater than one million yen, and he could only raise about one million yen of the money to give them.

He knew the hostage would only be released if the payment appeared to satisfy the demand. A bag visibly containing just the one million yen would either be recognized as short or, worse, signal that he was holding back money—putting him and the hostage at risk. So he added more cash of his own, bringing the bag's total above one million yen but still short of the demanded amount.

The purpose of the added cash was deceptive bulk: it made the pile of money look plausible as the larger demanded sum, so that at the handover the extortionists would glance at the thick bundle, assume the demand had been met, and release the hostage without carefully counting. By the time they discovered the shortfall, the exchange would already be complete. He accepted losing all the cash, including the extra he had added, since the bag was to be handed over and kept—his goal was to get the hostage released, not to recover the money.
